title: Ines and the Choir
premise: Ines 'Ulyana' Pemberton keeps the ledgers of the Cartographers' Guild, a quiet order that maps and trades in impossible things while pretending to be mere record-keepers. When a prophecy written a century ago surfaces bearing tonight's date and her own name beside a figure called the Choir's Voice, Ines realizes the guild has been hiding a living weapon: a chorus of bound spirits whose song can unmake borders—and armies. As the usurper Vessia marches on the free cities, Ines must choose between the guild's doctrine of invisibility and the truth that survival bought with silence is just another form of corruption. She ends by freeing the Choir at terrible cost, exposing the guild's complicity, and carrying the secret of the prophecy's true author to her grave—trading her own name into legend so the free cities can rebuild without another war.
about_author: Mara Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers in coastal trading cities before turning to fiction. Her novels blend bureaucratic precision with folkloric wonder, exploring what institutions bury to survive.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Ines Pemberton catalogs an impossible compass for the Guild of Unmapped Realms, establishing her role as keeper of secrets no one may speak. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility, faintly suffocating.

chapters.title: Tonight's Date
chapters.summary: Ines finds tonight's date inked in a century-old prophecy ledger, alongside her birth-name and the phrase 'the Choir's Voice.' Her mentor Halvard dismisses it as a clerical echo. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: What the Guild Trades
chapters.summary: A buyer arrives seeking something the ledgers say doesn't exist; Ines watches Halvard lie fluently and begins auditing old entries. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Choir
chapters.summary: Following discrepancies in the maps, Ines descends into the sealed undercroft and discovers the Choir: seven bound spirits whose harmonized song rewrites geography itself. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Vessia Crosses the Salt
chapters.summary: News arrives that usurper-queen Vessia has taken the Salt Marches; refugees bring rumors she hunts 'a voice' to finish an ancient conquest. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the abstract becomes urgent.

chapters.title: Halvard's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Ines confronts Halvard; he admits the guild bound the Choir a century ago to end the last war, then buried the sin along with the prophecy's author. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief for a mentor revealed as jailer.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Ines meets Tam, a runaway choir-tuner who escaped the undercroft years ago and knows how the binding works—and how it breaks. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people trained to disappear.

chapters.title: Ledgers Burned
chapters.summary: Someone torches the archive wing; Ines saves one volume—the prophecy—and realizes the guild will kill to keep its secret rather than face Vessia. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: betrayal hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Send No One
chapters.summary: Ines travels to Corvane to warn the city council; they refuse to act without proof, and a Vessian spy marks her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: institutional cowardice mirroring the guild's.

chapters.title: Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Fleeing Corvane, Ines pays a smuggler with a mapped impossibility from the ledgers, feeling the corruption of power use her for the first time. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: guilt as tuition.

chapters.title: Tam's Song
chapters.summary: Tam teaches Ines a fragment of the Choir's music; when she hums it, a river briefly changes course. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: intoxication and terror of power.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Cartographer
chapters.summary: Captured by Vessian scouts, Ines meets Sarel, Vessia's own mapmaker, who offers partnership: map the new world together after the conquest. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation of complicity dressed as safety.

chapters.title: What Vessia Wants
chapters.summary: Brought before Vessia, Ines learns the usurper seeks not destruction but the Choir—to sing the free cities into her empire without a battle. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: horror at mercy weaponized.

chapters.title: Escape by Unmapping
chapters.summary: Using a stolen fragment of song, Ines unmakes the road behind her and escapes with Tam's help, leaving soldiers stranded in unmapped country. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: survival purchased with others' suffering.

chapters.title: Return to the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Ines returns to find Halvard dying and the guild council preparing to surrender the Choir to Vessia as tribute. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the institution chooses survival over soul.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Author
chapters.summary: Dying Halvard reveals the prophecy was written by the Choir itself—a warning the guild chose to read as permission. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: every certainty inverted.

chapters.title: Council of Knives
chapters.summary: Ines appeals to the guild council; they vote to hand her to Vessia as the 'Voice' the prophecy demands. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: loyalty severed cleanly, like a ledger line.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: With Tam, Ines enters the undercroft and begins unbinding the Choir, each spirit freed demanding a price: a memory, a name, a future. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice made concrete and irrevocable.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Vessia's army surrounds the guildhall; the council opens the gates as Ines and Tam fight through the collapsing undercroft. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: chaos, urgency, no clean choices left.

chapters.title: The Voice Made Whole
chapters.summary: Climax: Ines joins the freed Choir's final song, erasing Vessia's claim-maps and dissolving her army's certainty mid-march—but the song demands the singer's name as payment. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: transcendence at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of an Unwritten Name
chapters.summary: Vessia's empire of paper collapses; the free cities credit a nameless hero, and Tam alone remembers who paid the price. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Tam founds a guild that maps honestly, records the whole truth of the Choir, and leaves the first page blank—for whoever hears the song next. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; memory as resistance.
